title: NCAR's DICast wind forecasts cut Xcel Energy's forecast error to 10.8%; Xcel estimates US$49 million saved
summary: NCAR's adaptive forecast-blending system (DICast), used by Xcel Energy since 2009, cut mean wind forecast error from about 18% to 10.8% by 2014; Xcel estimated US$49m saved (IEEE Spectrum 2015).
account: Sue Ellen Haupt and William Mahoney of the National Center for Atmospheric Research wrote in IEEE Spectrum (22 October 2015) that NCAR's wind power forecasting system for Xcel Energy blends numerical weather models with the Dynamic Integrated foreCast (DICast) system, used for wind prediction since 2009, which constantly checks its predictions against outcomes and adjusts its bias corrections and weightings; the mean forecast error at a typical wind farm fell from about 18 percent in 2008 to 10.8 percent by 2014, and Xcel estimated the improvements had saved customers US$49 million so far. A UCAR news item (7 February 2012) said the system saved ratepayers $6 million in 2010 alone and described the work as building on NCAR research ranging from statistics to artificial intelligence. E&E News (4 December 2017) quoted Haupt that the forecasts could save $10 million a year and reported that Xcel operators decommit large coal units when sustained wind is predicted. None of the sources describes the system as machine learning in so many words, and the savings are Xcel's estimates reported through NCAR and the press, not a regulator's audit.
purpose: The system was built to forecast wind generation for Xcel's unit-commitment and trading decisions; the cost savings are its intended use.
system: NCAR wind power forecasting system with the DICast adaptive forecast blending engine
developer: National Center for Atmospheric Research (Research Applications Laboratory)

ratings.reason: Xcel's US$49 million estimate and the error reduction to 10.8% are reported by the makers and the press without independent measurement.
Ratepayer savings and coal-unit decommitment are reported as estimates; no audited figure is documented.

ai_role.statement: The forecasting system's contribution to savings is Xcel's own estimate relayed by NCAR authors and reporters; the AI character of the system rests on UCAR's reference to artificial-intelligence research and DICast's adaptive bias correction, not on an explicit machine-learning description, so both the AI status and the causal share are unverified.

headline: NCAR's DICast cuts Xcel's wind forecast error to 10.8%
metric: cut mean wind forecast error from about 18% to 10.8% by 2014; Xcel estimated US$49m saved

comparator.against: Xcel's wind forecasts in 2008, before NCAR's system
comparator.before: about 18 percent for 18 to 42 hours ahead
comparator.quote: In 2008, the year we started working on this problem, the forecast error at a typical wind farm in this region was about 18 percent for 18 to 42 hours ahead, calculated as a percentage of the capacity of each farm. But by 2014, the mean forecast error had fallen to 10.8 percent.

later.note: By 2017 Xcel was still relying on the NCAR forecasts, which Haupt said saved about $10 million a year in production costs, while it planned coal retirements and more wind.
later.quote: According to Haupt, the forecasts, preparations and timing meant the company could save $10 million in power production costs each year.
